newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia c. bank says rupiah now in normal range.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia c. bank says rupiah now in normal range.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank said on Tuesday the rupiah had returned to a normal trading range in recent days after reaching a record low last week in the wake of an attack by speculators.

Paul Soetopo, a director of Bank Indonesia, told reporters that after reaching a low of 2,663 rupiah against the dollar on July 21, the currency had in recent days reached a normal level of between 2,555 and 2,610 rupiah.
"Under current conditions, the range is considered normal," Soetopo said.
He said Indonesia's economic fundamentals were strong with a high rate of growth, falling inflation and foreign reserves which continued to increase.
"Actually the exchange rate of the rupiah has a tendency to remain strong," Soetopo said.
"As such, the fluctuation of the rupiah in recent days is more influenced by technical factors, that is the contagion effect, or speculation by foreign hedge funds," he said.

Soetopo said as foreign currency markets were inter-connected, it was expected that this contagion effect would continue although policies to support marco-economic stability would continue to be implemented.

"For the time being, it is hoped all sides, inlcuding banking, business and the community in general, will consider this matter more calmly to support the stability of the rupiah's foreign exchange rate," he said.
The rupiah came under attack after a period of instability in Southeast Asian currencies triggered by the devaluation of the Thai baht at the beginning of the month.
